title: Auto-Resume After Limits
bottom_line: Turn on /auto-resume and a session stopped by the usage limit gets continue typed into it once the limit resets, so long runs continue.

sections.heading: Type /auto-resume on, off, alone, or inside a prompt

blocks.title: What to type
blocks.caption: The first line switches it for every session, or shows its state when typed alone. The second adds it to one prompt only.

blocks.title: The four ways to use it
rows: Resume every session automatically. Kept across restarts.
Auto-resume is on for every session.
Turn it off for every session and cancel the pending `continue` in the session where you type it.
Auto-resume is off for every session.

Resume only the task that prompt starts, for example `/plan-tools:plan-implement-complete plan.md /auto-resume`. The word is removed before the prompt or command runs. The task ends at the next prompt you type without it.
The prompt or command runs without the word.
Show whether it is on and when the next `continue` is due.
Auto-resume is on for every session, on for the current task, or off, then Next "continue" at a time when one is pending.

blocks.text: The mod types `continue` into a session that stopped on the usage limit (the 5-hour session limit or the weekly limit), once that limit resets. Long unattended runs, such as `/plan-tools:plan-implement-complete`, pick up where they stopped.
In Claude Code's command list, `/auto-resume` is described as: Send "continue" when a usage limit resets: on, off, or add /auto-resume to a prompt for that task only.

sections.heading: You need a mod-loading Claude Code and a claude.ai subscription

cards.title: Claude Code that loads mods
cards.text: The plugin registers a TypeScript module through `hooks/hooks.json`, not a skill, so your Claude Code version must load plugin mods.

cards.title: A claude.ai subscription
cards.text: With it, Claude Code reports the rate-limit windows and their reset times, which the mod needs.

blocks.title: Nothing to configure
items: State is kept in the plugin's own store.

sections.heading: Choose every session or just one task

cards.title: Every session
cards.text: Type `/auto-resume on`. Every session is resumed automatically, and the setting is kept across restarts. Type `/auto-resume off` to stop.

cards.title: One task only
cards.text: Add `/auto-resume` to the prompt that starts the task. The word is removed before the prompt or command runs.

blocks.title: How the one-task form behaves
items: Only the task that prompt starts is resumed.
The task ends at the next prompt you type without `/auto-resume`.
The word only counts as a separate word, with a space or the edge of the line on each side.
It works with a slash command too, for example `/plan-tools:plan-implement-complete plan.md /auto-resume`.

sections.heading: Continue is sent three minutes after the limit resets

steps.title: The main conversation hits the limit
steps.text: The main conversation stops with a `rate_limit` error. Limits hit by subagents are ignored; only the main conversation's stop counts.

steps.title: It finds the reset time
steps.text: It reads the windows Claude Code reports and takes the latest reset time among the exhausted ones. The status line shows `auto-resume at <time>`.

steps.title: It waits three minutes past the reset
steps.text: The wait lets Claude Code's built-in auto-continue go first. If anything starts a turn before then (the built-in auto-continue or you), the pending `continue` is dropped.

steps.title: It types continue
steps.text: It submits `continue` as a normal prompt, and the session picks up where it stopped. A `continue` that hits the limit again schedules the next one.

items.label: Wait after the reset
items.note: lets the built-in auto-continue go first

items.label: Retry when no reset time
items.note: used when Claude Code reports no reset time

items.label: Clock check interval
items.note: a laptop that slept through the reset catches up when it wakes

sections.heading: Check the status line or type /auto-resume alone

blocks.title: Two places to look
rows: The status line, while a `continue` is pending
Whether it is on, and when the next `continue` is due

blocks.title: Replies to /auto-resume alone
items: Auto-resume is on for every session.
Auto-resume is on for the current task.
When a `continue` is pending, the reply adds Next "continue" at followed by the time, shown as a short weekday with hour and minute.

sections.heading: Keep the session open, or reopen it with claude --resume

cards.title: The terminal was closed
cards.text: It can only type into a session that is open. If you close the terminal, the pending `continue` is saved.

points.text: It fires when you reopen that session with `claude --resume`.

cards.title: A subagent hit the limit
cards.text: Limits hit by subagents are ignored. Only the main conversation's stop counts.

cards.title: The usage message appeared
cards.text: Any argument other than on or off replies Usage: /auto-resume on | off, or add /auto-resume to a prompt.

cards.title: You typed before it fired
cards.text: If anything starts a turn before the `continue` is due, including you or the built-in auto-continue, the pending `continue` is dropped.

next_action.text: Type `/auto-resume on` to resume every session automatically.
next_action.detail: Or add `/auto-resume` to one prompt to cover only the task it starts.
